newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan key 3-month CD rate falls to 0.53 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan key 3-month CD rate falls to 0.53 pct.

text.p: The rate on key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) in Tokyo fell to 0.53 percent in Tuesday afternoon trade, the lowest issued rate for the CDs since December 22, traders said.
The issued volume was about 20 billion yen.
The key CDs were last issued at 0.54 percent on Friday.

"A consensus was formed in the money market that the yield curve of one-, two- and three-month CD rates may remain flat for the time being. That was behind the new issues of the three-month CDs today," said a city bank dealer.
One- and two-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent, both unchanged from the levels they were issued at previously. They were issued in volumes of 30 billion yen each, traders said.
News that the United States had launched a cruise missile attack against Iraq pulled down Euroyen futures.
But the news failed to have a strong impact on cash money market rates, traders said.

Key March three-month Euroyen interest rate futures dropped to finish at 99.06, down from Monday's 99.14, due to fears that the yen would fall against the dollar and expectations of a rise in U.S. short-term rates. But cash three-month Euroyen rates fell to 0.53125 percent from Monday's 0.55 percent.
"In the cash money market so far, the U.S. attack has been considered a performance by (President Bill) Clinton ahead of the presidential election," the dealer said.
